I am writing regarding the Cycle Inspection Report for 2344 S. Zona Court, File No. 10539, and the October 9, 2026 deadline for completing the identified corrections.

However, the receptacle is controlled by a wall switch and therefore receives power only when that switch is turned on.

Could you please confirm whether the switch may have been off when the receptacle was inspected or whether the switch-controlled configuration itself was the reason it was identified as nonfunctioning or incorrectly wired? If the configuration must be changed, please let me know what correction is required so that I can provide the electrician with precise instructions and ensure that the work fully satisfies the inspection requirement.

I would also be grateful if you could clarify which window contains the deteriorated lower rail referenced in the report.

Please let me know whether the requested extension can be approved and whether there are any forms or additional steps I should complete.

Thank you for your consideration and assistance.

Sincerely,

Osundwa Wanjera

DUPLICATE of ROW2026-09-2763 . Roto-Rooter will provide 2 technicians and 1 operator to replace the entire sewer line outside the foundation of the home, out to the city street, connecting to the existing city tap. The street will need to be shut down, and Roto-Rooter will obtain the permits required for proper road and sidewalk closure. Roto-Rooter will use street signs, fencing, plates, and cones to close the street and sidewalk for the safety of technicians, motor vehicles, and pedestrians. Roto-Rooter will remove the city street and dig up to 5 ft to expose the city main and tap.

The existing line leaving the house is cast iron transitioning into clay tile. Roto-Rooter will remove two squares of city sidewalk and use an excavator to trench along the existing line path from the city street all the way to the house. The old cast iron and clay tile will be removed and replaced with new pipe.

The new line will be checked for structural integrity, and grade will follow the existing line path. After the line has been fully installed with a new two-directional cleanout, it will be tested thoroughly. Roto-Rooter will then backfill the trench properly in the yard, leaving a mound to help with the earth's settlement. Roto-Rooter is not responsible for the settling of the earth. Roto-Rooter will use the city-mandated amount of flowable fill, and the proper height and thickness of concrete and asphalt, to close the roadway back up. Street plates will be used to open the roadway after hours and to cover the asphalt while it settles.

All asphalt and concrete sidewalk restoration will be performed by a licensed subcontractor hired by Roto-Rooter. The subcontractor is solely responsible for the workmanship, materials, cure time, and finish of the asphalt and sidewalk work, as well as any warranty on that work. Scheduling of the restoration is subject to the subcontractor's availability and weather conditions and may occur after the sewer line work is complete

The Great Inflatable Race is a family friendly event for the community to enjoy with a focus on having fun while raising money and food for Hoosier Hills Food Bank. Racers do pay to register ahead of time which covers their inflatable costume to race in and their swag bag they receive. There is no charge to attend the event otherwise. There are 100 racers total.  10 racers race at a time. The winner from each leg moves forward to the final race. There will be a vendor alley market inside the pavilion, 4 main bounce houses on the pavilion lawn. A bubble station and coloring competition station next to a main stage on the pavilion lawn as well as four Hoosier hills food bank tables to collect donations. We will have a live radio broadcast with B97 during the race itself 2pm-4pm and an MC outside of the broadcast. Event starts at noon and ends at 6pm.
